readiness_rule.move_to_march: Average below 515, any repeated unfinished section, or a persistent section below 126 at the confirmed 30-day deadline.

Start: Wednesday, August 19, 2026  |  Target score: 520  |  Content load: 20-22 hr/week

blocks.label: Decision
blocks.text: Run the January-first calendar now. Use the registered late-January date as the anchor once the 2027 calendar opens; move to March only if the evidence-based checkpoint says January is unlikely to produce the target score.

blocks.label: Calendar status
blocks.text: As of August 17, 2026, the official AAMC pages still show the 2026 testing calendar. January 22-23 are placeholders, not claimed test dates. Begin checking October 1 and register the day the 2027 dates open.

items: The plan now starts Wednesday, August 19; no work is treated as already completed.
The diagnostic is Saturday, August 22, and the first scored third-party full-length is Saturday, October 3.
Kaplan is a diagnostic-dependent reference: full reading is reserved for low-confidence material.
UWorld rises to a 900-1,100 evidence-driven range; all 600 AAMC Section Bank questions are scheduled before the dense official-exam run.
CARS begins with the full nine-passage diagnostic section in Week 1, ramps to roughly two per day by Week 6, and reaches three per day or equivalent in the official phase.
Weeks 11, 15, and 19 contain protected float capacity; later review topics come from the mistake log, not preassigned favorite chapters.
Take the AAMC Unscored Sample as a low-pressure baseline. Classify each topic 0-3 for confidence and use that evidence to change the assigned study mode.
Pair every learning block with topic-mode questions. Count questions that were reviewed deeply, not screens completed.
Log wrong, flagged, and guessed-correct items. Record the cause, one concrete fix, and a retest due 7-14 days later.
Do not stack a normal UWorld quota on top of a full-length. The exam and its review are the week's main practice volume.
Anki is capped at 30-45 minutes on six days per week. Default deck: AnKing MCAT; create only selective cards from actual gaps.
Use the approximately 100-page Khan-Academy-derived Psych/Soc document with the AAMC content outline; do not rely on the older Kaplan P/S terminology alone.

blocks.text: If March becomes the test date

items: Do not restart content review. Use the mistake log and mastery checklist to select at most three repair themes per week.
Reduce full-length frequency to every 2-3 weeks, preserve remaining official exams for the final month, and use two timed sections in non-FL weeks.
Maintain CARS at roughly three passages per day, Anki at 30-45 minutes, and one full rest day each week.

October 1, 2026: begin checking the AAMC registration page and email updates. Register on the day 2027 dates open; test-center capacity is first-come, first-served.
Activate a 180-day UWorld subscription on or after August 17 if purchasing it for this plan; it covers a late-January test with margin.
Kaplan 2019-2020 remains acceptable for foundational sciences. For P/S terminology and research methods, cross-check the AAMC content outline and Khan Academy-derived P/S document.
After registration, replace every placeholder date in schedule.csv and regenerate the workbook/guide before changing study blocks manually.

mistakeLog.sourceNote: Log wrong, flagged, and guessed-correct questions only. Name the cause, choose one concrete fix, and set a retest due date 7-14 days later.

weeklyPatternReview.sourceNote: At the end of each week, select no more than three recurring patterns. Turn each pattern into a concrete action and a dated retest.

mastery.sourceNote: Confidence: 0 = unfamiliar, 1 = recognize, 2 = explain, 3 = apply. Mastery requires delayed retrieval and application.
